question: When is it allowed to park or stop on a freeway shoulder?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:Any time if you turn on hazard flashers.,c:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
note: Parking or stopping on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergencies.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They can stop quickly if needed,b:They are always required to stay out of the road,c:They always follow traffic rules,d:Children lack adult reflexes and are smaller/harder to see
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; give them extra space near schools, parks, and neighborhoods.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a note with your name, address, and report to police.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Call your insurance company when you get home.
note: If you strike parked property, leave your contact information securely attached to the vehicle or property you hit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best practice?
options: a:Proceed very slowly and wait for a gap.,b:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of traffic and merge safely.,c:Turn on hazard lights while merging.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.
note: Use the acceleration lane to get up to freeway speed so you can merge smoothly with existing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The largest vehicle goes first,b:The vehicle on your left has the right-of-way,c:The vehicle on your right has the right-of-way,d:You should always wait until there are no vehicles
note: When multiple vehicles arrive together at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: Which device or activity increases a driver's crash risk due to distraction?
options: a:Cell phone use.,b:Listening to the radio at normal volume.,c:Operating the CD player briefly.
note: Using a cell phone (even hands-free) or other audio devices can greatly distract drivers and raise crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian waves.,b:Only if the pedestrian is paying attention.,c:At all times.,d:Only when the pedestrian has a hand signal.
note: You must stop and yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian in a crosswalk; only proceed when your lane is clear and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, who should yield?
options: a:You should yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:You may force your way into traffic.
note: Vehicles entering from driveways or private roads must yield to traffic already on the public roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right yields to the left,b:The faster vehicle goes first,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right,d:The larger vehicle has the right-of-way
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: What is a common effect of continuous hard braking on ice and snow?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Continuous hard braking on icy or snowy roads can lock wheels and cause a loss of steering control.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:They are eliminated if you have two outside mirrors.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:You can check blind spots with rearview mirrors alone.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

question: What does an orange-colored road sign generally warn of?
options: a:A railroad crossing is ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.
note: Orange signs indicate construction or maintenance work zones; exercise extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about stopping in a travel lane is correct?
options: a:You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason.,b:You may stop to drop off passengers in a travel lane.,c:You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong freeway ramp.,d:All of the above are unsafe and generally illegal.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane; if you miss a turn or exit, continue to a safe place to turn around rather than backing up.

question: On slick or slippery roads, how should you take turns?
options: a:Brake hard in the middle of the turn.,b:Accelerate through the turn.,c:Change lanes quickly before turning.,d:Take turns more slowly than usual.
note: Reduce speed and negotiate turns more slowly on slick surfaces to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When your slow speed disrupts normal traffic flow.,b:When driving in a work zone at night.,c:Only on rural roads.,d:When following large trucks.
note: You must not drive so slowly that you interfere with the normal flow of traffic; doing so can result in a citation.

question: When is it acceptable to cross a dashed (broken) white line?
options: a:Only during daylight.,b:When you need to pass and it is safe.,c:At any time.,d:Only in emergencies.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure to change lanes?
options: a:Only signal if other traffic is present,b:Check mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes,c:Check mirror and change lanes without signaling,d:Signal then immediately change lanes without checking mirrors
note: Signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and the target lane, and change lanes when safe.

question: Should you avoid driving beside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots on both sides; avoid driving alongside them for long periods and either drop back or move ahead.

question: What is the correct technique for backing a vehicle?
options: a:Rely only on mirrors while backing.,b:Open your door to see whether it is safe to reverse.,c:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing slowly.
note: When backing, look directly through the rear window and proceed slowly; don't rely solely on mirrors.

question: Which substances may lead to arrest for DUII or impair driving?
options: a:Beer, wine, and other liquor,b:Illegal drugs and some prescription medicines,c:Inhalants like glue or paint,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications can impair driving and result in DUII charges.

question: On the road, bicycles are considered:
options: a:Vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.,b:Hazards that must always yield to cars.,c:Not subject to the rules of the road.
note: Bicycles are vehicles and bicyclists must follow the same rules as motor vehicle drivers.

question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog to improve visibility?
options: a:Yes — high beams always improve vision,b:No — use low beams or fog lights,c:Yes — but only on rural roads,d:No — turn headlights off and use parking lights
note: In fog or mist, use low beam headlights or fog lights; high beams reflect back and decrease visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and confirming it is safe to proceed.,b:After slowing down to check for cross traffic only.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
note: If a stop sign has no marked line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where all corners have stop signs, who should yield the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you,b:The driver on your left,c:The driver across from you,d:The largest vehicle
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive; if multiple arrive together, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors there are blind spots; turn your head and glance over your shoulder to check them before changing lanes.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Low beam headlights improve your visibility to others and reduce glare in rain or fog; do not use high beams.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, you should drive more slowly and turn on:
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Emergency flashers.,c:Headlights.,d:Interior dome light.
note: Use headlights when visibility is poor so others can see you; increase speed only when safe or pull off if necessary.

question: What can cause 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Too much sleep the night before your trip.
note: 'Highway hypnosis' can occur when you stare straight ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning, causing you to zone out.

question: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, you should:
options: a:Only have a general idea of where you're going.,b:Rely only on road signs to find your way.,c:Depend solely on a passenger to give directions.,d:Plan your route in advance.
note: Plan your trip before you go so you are not distracted or uncertain while driving in unfamiliar areas.

question: True or false: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you begin braking.
options: a:True.,b:False.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance; as speed rises, the distance needed to stop grows significantly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle using lights or a siren?
options: a:When you hear a siren or see flashing red or blue lights.,b:Only if other drivers yield first.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle that is using its siren or flashing lights.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Two-way left-turn lane ahead.,b:Passing permitted when no oncoming traffic.,c:Prepare to stop for pedestrian crossing.,d:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction except for permitted left turns.

question: What is the correct method to check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, then look over the shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter.,b:Only turn and look over your right shoulder regardless of direction.,c:Trust that outside mirrors eliminate blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check all mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator to create space between you and the vehicle ahead without sudden braking or swerving.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, check traffic, and gradually steer back onto the roadway when safe.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Stop and wait for assistance.
note: Reduce speed, scan for traffic, and carefully re-enter the roadway when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and return safely.,c:Back up on the shoulder.,d:Signal and reverse into the exit.
note: Do not stop or back up on a highway; continue to the next exit and re-route safely.

question: You should always use your turn signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above.
note: Use your turn signal to communicate your intentions whenever changing lanes, entering traffic, or leaving parking areas.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before lane changes called?
options: a:A good driving habit.,b:A bad driving habit.,c:Unnecessary.
note: Looking over your shoulder to check blind spots is a proper and necessary driving habit before lane changes.

question: If you're in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Only move your vehicle if no one is harmed,b:Ignore and continue driving,c:Leave the scene immediately,d:Stop at the scene, help injured, and call police if needed
note: Stop immediately, move the vehicle if safe, call police and ambulance if necessary, and assist the injured without moving them unnecessarily.

question: Regulatory signs are typically what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Blue.,d:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs are usually white with black markings and indicate legal requirements such as speed limits and turn restrictions.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on at night and it's hard to see, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the vehicle passes.,b:Look straight ahead, keeping your lane.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: Avoid looking directly at bright headlights; glance to the right edge of your lane and watch from peripheral vision.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do with your vehicle lights?
options: a:Use parking lights.,b:Use four-way flashers at all times.,c:Turn on your headlights (low beam).
note: At dusk or on overcast days you must use headlights; dim to low beams near other vehicles.

question: Which behavior helps prevent crashes by making your actions predictable to others?
options: a:Drive only on side streets and back roads.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Communicate with other road users.
note: Signal your intentions and use warnings like horns or lights when appropriate to reduce unexpected actions and crashes.

question: Why must you use extra caution when approaching a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:He or she is a police officer.,b:He or she is deaf.,c:He or she is blind or visually impaired.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates the pedestrian is blind or visually impaired; yield and take extra care to avoid harm.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Accelerate to regain control,b:Turn sharply back onto the pavement immediately,c:Open your door and inspect the tire,d:Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and brake gently; wait until speed is reduced to re-enter the roadway safely.

question: A solid white centerline on a multi-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed.,c:Center turn lane ahead.,d:Parking allowed on either side.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes going the same direction and indicate lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.

question: If you see pedestrians near the road, you should:
options: a:Speed up to clear the area.,b:Sound your horn and continue.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.,d:Drive into the opposing lane to avoid them.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, reduce speed and be prepared to stop for their safety.

question: When you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Slow down and continue driving.,c:Motion for it to pass you.
note: Immediately pull to the right and stop for approaching emergency vehicles using lights or sirens; if in an intersection, clear it first.

question: Are roads especially slippery when it first starts to rain?
options: a:True — oil and dirt on the road make it especially slippery at first,b:False — rain always improves traction,c:True — only on highways,d:False — only with heavy rain
note: Roads can be extra slippery when rain first begins due to oil and debris mixing with water; reduce speed accordingly.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:Lower your ability to concentrate on driving.,b:Decrease chances of an accident.,c:Cause you to fall asleep at the wheel.,d:Improve reaction time.
note: Strong emotions and stress can reduce concentration and decision-making, increasing crash risk.
